identity.name: Visigoths
alt_names: Gothic army of Alaric and Athaulf

land.text: Thessaly, where Alaric's forces were sent after Theodosius's death in 395

predecessors.note: The Goths themselves came from the Danube federates of the Eastern Empire (the gothia and goths rows); the page gives no earlier land.

land.text: the Garonne valley of Gallia Aquitania in which Honorius settled Wallia's federates in 418: 'the Visigoths were settled as foederati in southern Gaul, establishing a kingdom with its capital at Toulouse'

successors.note: visigothic-kingdom (418-721) is the same people as a settled kingdom; Cliopatria's Visigoths row runs to 425 and its Visigothic Kingdom row begins in 426, so this dossier stops at the settlement and the kingdom's own dossier carries 418-425.

capitals.name: Toulouse
capitals.note: The only seat the page gives: 'establishing a kingdom with its capital at Toulouse' (418). Before that the Goths are an army on the move (Greece, Italy, Gaul, Hispania) with no capital.

rulers.name: Alaric I
rulers.note: Infobox reign 395-410; the page text has him die at Consentia in the early months of 411, the Sack of Rome page in late 410.

rulers.name: Athaulf
rulers.note: Reigned 411-415; killed at Barcelona on 15 August 415.

rulers.name: Sigeric (Segeric)
rulers.note: Chosen after Athaulf's murder and assassinated the same year.

rulers.name: Wallia
rulers.note: 'Wallia was chosen to replace Sigeric in 415'; died in 418, succeeded by Theodoric I (visigothic-kingdom).

correction.text: Thessaly, the Goths' first ground after Theodosius's death

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria begins in 396. The page: 'Modern writers regard Alaric as king of the Visigoths from 395' and 'the Visigoths ... were first united under Alaric I (395-410)' (Visigoths page); per Burns, Alaric's forces were sent to Thessaly in 395 'No battle took place'. Presence zone, not a border. No infobox area on either page.

19,756 km2 in Attica and the north Peloponnese. 'In 396, he marched through Thermopylae and sacked Athens'; Claudian has his troops plunder 'for the next year or so as far south as the mountainous Peloponnese'. A plunder zone, not held land (the provinces stay Eastern Roman).

correction.text: Epirus, to which Stilicho pushed Alaric's forces; Alaric's command in Illyricum from 397

keyframe_review.note: 44,637 km2, bbox 19.2-24.1 E and 36.7-40.8 N: Epirus, Thessaly and the Peloponnese. The page: Stilicho's attack 'stemmed the plundering as he pushed Alaric's forces north into Epirus', and in 397 Arcadius made Alaric magister militum per Illyricum (Visigoths page: 'named military commander of the eastern Illyrian prefecture'); the province was 'nominally transferred' to the West after Eutropius fell in 399. So the Peloponnese leaves the shape in 397 and Epirus (12,392 km2) is the ground.

correction.text: the Po valley around Pollentia and Verona in Alaric's campaign of 402

keyframe_review.note: 144 cells: a Po-valley part (24,500 km2, 8.0-12.3 E) and a Greek remnant. The page: 'Alaric's attack actually began in late 401', Stilicho beat him at Pollentia ('on Easter Sunday') and again at Verona in 402. The Greek remnant is dropped; the Po valley stands for 402 only, because after Verona Stilicho 'allowed Alaric to withdraw' into Pannonia.

New keyframe for 403-406 (Cliopatria keeps the 402 shape to 406). The page: after Verona 'withdrawal into Pannonia', and 'Between 404 and 405, Alaric remained in one of the four Pannonian provinces' with a magister militum's codicils from Stilicho. The Hungarian country stands for western Pannonia (gazetteer lacks Pannonia, so the country is over-large and east of the Danube too).

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid for 408-409 only: Rome and its province under blockade

keyframe_review.note: 4,097 km2 around Rome (11.7-12.8 E, 41.7-42.5 N, the province of Roma). The Sack page: 'The Goths under Alaric laid siege to the city in late 408', lifted in December 408 after the ransom, 'Alaric took Portus and renewed the siege of Rome in late 409'. So the shape is right for 408-409; for 407 Alaric was in Noricum (visigoths_407b). [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 408..409 from this entry's own 'valid for 408-409 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

New keyframe: 'During this crisis in 407, Alaric again marched on Italy, taking a position in Noricum (modern Austria), where he demanded a sum of 4,000 pounds of gold.' Austria stands for Noricum (gazetteer lacks it).

union.text: Campania, Lucania and Calabria, ravaged after the sack of Rome

correction.text: valid for 410 only: Rome and its province until the sack of 24-26 August 410, then the south of Italy, Campania, Lucania and Calabria, that Alaric ravaged in the autumn

keyframe_review.note: 5,027 km2 around Rome for 410-413. Right for 410 only: 'On 24 August 410 the Visigoths entered Rome through its Salarian Gate' and pillaged it three days; then Alaric 'headed for southern Italy'.

correction.text: Campania, Lucania and Calabria, ravaged after the sack of Rome

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'The Visigoths ravaged Campania, Lucania, and Calabria'; Alaric died at Consentia in Bruttium (early 411 on the Alaric page, late 410 on the Sack page); the ships for Sicily and Africa 'were wrecked by a storm' at the Strait of Messina. Presence zone only.

New keyframe: 'In the spring of 412, Constantius pressed Athaulf' and he 'led his followers out of Italy and north into a temporarily pacified Gaul'; he 'took possession of Narbonne and Toulouse in 413'. In 412 the Goths are on the road (the page names no ground), so 412 has no shape and the 413 cities are soft.

correction.text: Narbonne, Toulouse and Bordeaux, the cities Athaulf held

keyframe_review.note: 12,698 km2 round Narbonne for 414-416. Right in kind for 414: Athaulf married Galla Placidia at Narbonne in January 414 and in 414 'acclaimed Priscus Attalus as Augustus at Bordeaux'; the Cliopatria shape runs from Narbonne to Toulouse (1.4-3.3 E) but does not reach Bordeaux. In 415 the Goths withdrew into Hispania, so the shape holds for 414 only.

correction.text: Barcelona and northern Hispania, where Athaulf withdrew in 415

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In 415, Athaulf withdrew with his people into northern Hispania' and was killed at Barcelona (15 August 415). Wallia accepted Honorius's treaty in 416 (Wallia page) and the page puts no ground to 416; the Barcelona area is carried to 416 as a bridge.

correction.text: Baetica and Lusitania, where Wallia's federates fought the Vandals and Alans

keyframe_review.note: 35,100 km2 in Aquitaine for 417-425. The page: in 417-418 Wallia's Goths, 'acting as foederati, fought the Alans and Vandals in Baetica and Lusitania' and were then recalled; they were settled in the Garonne valley only in 418 ('The Goths were settled ... from Toulouse to Bordeaux and the Atlantic coastal strip from Les Landes to the Loire' on the Wallia page; 'In 418' on the Visigoths page). So the shape is right from 418, as visigothic-kingdom_418, and for 417-418 the Goths' ground is Hispania.

ledger.note: 395: the Goths are united under Alaric. 'they were first united under Alaric I (395-410)' (Visigoths page); his forces were sent to Thessaly, where 'No battle took place' (Alaric page). The year is the page's, Thessaly is the researcher's reading.
396: the Goths leave Thessaly for the south. 'In 396, he marched through Thermopylae and sacked Athens'; Thessaly is where Alaric's forces had been sent in 395.
396: Alaric plunders Greece. 'In 396, he marched through Thermopylae and sacked Athens', then plundered 'as far south as the mountainous Peloponnese'. A plunder zone, not annexed land.

397: Stilicho drives the Goths out of the south. His surprise attack 'stemmed the plundering as he pushed Alaric's forces north into Epirus' (no year on the page; the same year Arcadius made Alaric military commander).

397: Alaric is named military commander of Illyricum. 'In 397, Alaric was named military commander of the eastern Illyrian prefecture by Arcadius' (Visigoths page; the Alaric page: magister militum per Illyricum); Epirus is where Stilicho had pushed him.
401: the Goths leave Epirus for Italy. The page is silent on when they left; 'Alaric's attack actually began in late 401' (Halsall) and the Illyrian command had lapsed after Eutropius fell in 399.

region.text: the Po valley around Pollentia and Verona

ledger.note: 402: Alaric invades Italy. 'Alaric's attack actually began in late 401'; the two first met in Italy in 402, 'The first was at Pollentia on Easter Sunday' and Alaric was beaten again at Verona.
402: Alaric withdraws from Italy. Stilicho 'allowed Alaric to withdraw' (the page's 'withdrawal into Pannonia').

403: the Goths settle in Pannonia. 'Between 404 and 405, Alaric remained in one of the four Pannonian provinces' with a magister militum's codicils from Stilicho; the page gives no year for the move (after Verona, 402).
407: Alaric leaves Pannonia. The page is silent on the date; 'During this crisis in 407, Alaric again marched on Italy, taking a position in Noricum'.
407: Alaric takes a position in Noricum. 'During this crisis in 407, Alaric again marched on Italy, taking a position in Noricum (modern Austria), where he demanded a sum of 4,000 pounds of gold.'
408: Alaric marches from Noricum on Rome ('invasion in early October 408' on the Sack page; 'in September 408 he menaced the city' on the Alaric page).

408: Alaric besieges Rome. 'The Goths under Alaric laid siege to the city in late 408'; he lifted it and withdrew to Etruria in December 408 for a ransom of 5,000 pounds of gold, took Portus and renewed the siege in late 409 (Attalus proclaimed emperor).

region.text: Campania, Lucania and Calabria, ravaged after the sack of Rome

ledger.note: 410: the Goths ravage the south of Italy. 'The Visigoths ravaged Campania, Lucania, and Calabria'; Nola and perhaps Capua were sacked. The year is the page's (after August 410); the shape is the researcher's reading of three regions.
410: Alaric sacks Rome and leaves. 'On 24 August 410 the Visigoths entered Rome through its Salarian Gate' and pillaged for three days; 'Alaric quickly left Rome and headed for southern Italy'.

region.text: Campania, Lucania and Calabria, ravaged after the sack of Rome

ledger.note: 412: Athaulf leads the Goths out of Italy. 'In the spring of 412, Constantius pressed Athaulf'; he 'led his followers out of Italy and north into a temporarily pacified Gaul'.
413: the Goths hold Narbonne and Toulouse. 'Athaulf took possession of Narbonne and Toulouse in 413'; he also captured Jovinus at Valence in 413 and married Galla Placidia at Narbonne in January 414.
414: Athaulf proclaims Attalus at Bordeaux. 'In 414, Athaulf acclaimed Priscus Attalus as Augustus at Bordeaux'; the page does not date the capture of Bordeaux.

region.text: Narbonne, Toulouse and Bordeaux, the cities Athaulf held

ledger.note: 415: the Goths leave Gaul. 'In 415, Athaulf withdrew with his people into northern Hispania.'
415: the Goths are at Barcelona. Athaulf was killed in the palace at Barcelona on 15 August 415; Sigeric and then Wallia were chosen the same year.

417: Wallia's Goths leave the Barcelona area for the south. The page gives no ground for 416 (the treaty with Honorius, return of Galla Placidia) and has the campaign in Baetica and Lusitania from 417.

417: Wallia's Goths fall on the Vandals in Baetica. They fought 'the Alans and Vandals in Baetica and Lusitania' with 'dramatic success' and, Hydatius says, 'a vast slaughter' of the barbarians; the page dates the campaign 417-418.
417: Wallia's Goths fall on the Alans in Lusitania. They killed the Alan ruler Addax.
418: Constantius recalls the Goths. He 'recalled the Goths, possibly because he feared their success'; the page gives 418, Halsall 419.
418: the Goths leave Lusitania. The Alan ruler Addax is dead and the Goths are recalled; the page does not say who held Lusitania afterwards.

region.text: the Garonne valley, Toulouse to Bordeaux, settled in 418

ledger.note: 418: Honorius settles the Goths in Aquitaine. 'In 418, the Visigoths were settled as foederati in southern Gaul, establishing a kingdom with its capital at Toulouse' (they got 'land in Gallia Aquitania'); Wallia died in 418 and Theodoric I succeeded. The kingdom continues in visigothic-kingdom.

wars.name: Gothic campaign in Greece
wars.outcome: Alaric sacked Athens in 396 and plundered the Peloponnese until Stilicho's surprise attack pushed him north into Epirus; in 397 Arcadius made him military commander of Illyricum.
wars.note: The Alaric page: 'No battle took place' in Thessaly in 395.

wars.name: Alaric's invasion of Italy
wars.outcome: Stilicho beat Alaric at Pollentia (Easter 402) and at Verona; Alaric withdrew into Pannonia.

wars.name: Alaric's march on Rome
wars.outcome: Siege in late 408 ended with a ransom (December 408); the second siege from late 409 made Priscus Attalus emperor; Rome was sacked on 24-26 August 410 and the Goths went south.
wars.note: The Alaric page has Alaric die at Consentia in early 411, the Sack page in late 410.

wars.name: Athaulf's war in Gaul

zones.text: Narbonne, Toulouse and Bordeaux, the cities Athaulf held

wars.outcome: Athaulf took Narbonne and Toulouse (413), captured Jovinus at Valence, executed Sarus, married Galla Placidia (January 414), proclaimed Attalus at Bordeaux (414) and withdrew into Hispania in 415.

wars.name: Wallia's campaign in Hispania

zones.text: Baetica and Lusitania, where Wallia's federates fought the Vandals and Alans

wars.outcome: As Honorius's federates Wallia's Goths fought the Alans and Vandals in Baetica and Lusitania (the Alan ruler Addax was killed) and were recalled in 418, to be settled in Aquitaine.
wars.note: The Wallia page names the Asding Vandals, not the Silingi; the recall is 418, Halsall suggests 419.

certainty.note: An army and its people on the move: every shape is a presence zone, never a surveyed border; the 418 Aquitaine grant (visigothic-kingdom) is the first fixed ground.

notes:
Cliopatria's Visigoths row (396-425, seven shapes) is a track of presence zones: Greece, Epirus, the Po valley, Rome, then Narbonne and Aquitaine. Corrections: the 397 shape keeps only Epirus; 402 only the Po valley; 403-406 Pannonia and 407 Noricum are new; the Rome shape holds 408-410 (it is held to 413 in Cliopatria, but the Goths left Italy in spring 412 and were at Narbonne in 413); 411 southern Italy, 413 Narbonne and Toulouse (412 on the road, no shape), 414 Narbonne/Toulouse/Bordeaux, 415-416 Barcelona, 417-418 Baetica and Lusitania. The Aquitaine shape for 417-425 is correctly Visigothic only from the 418 settlement, and belongs to visigothic-kingdom (found 418) from then; so this dossier ends in 418 (the year both start/stop, the army in Spain until the recall, the kingdom from the settlement). Family 'iberia' follows visigothic-kingdom for colour continuity.
Pages disagree on Alaric's death (early 411 on the Alaric page text and infobox; late 410 on the Sack page) and on the siege of Rome of 408 (September on the Alaric page, 'late 408' on the Sack page, invasion in October). The Visigoths article gives none of 412-417 and no infobox with dates or area; the Wallia page names the Asding rather than the Silingi Vandals and dates the recall 418 (Halsall 419). Gazetteer lacks Pannonia and Noricum: Hungary and Austria stand in (both over-large). Unverified: the 416 location (page silent), the 401 departure from Epirus, the 403 move into Pannonia. Budget: five pages used (Visigoths, Alaric I, Wallia, Athaulf, Sack of Rome (410)).
The Roman federate treaty of 416 and the 418 foedus make the Goths a client of the western-roman-empire; the vassal event belongs on that dossier (the schema's vassal_start names the vassal as counterpart).
